# How does water reach the top of a plant?

<!-- STEP id="evaporate" -->
## Water leaves the leaf
Inside a leaf, water evaporates from the wet cells, and the water vapour passes out through open stomata into the air. This loss of water vapour through the stomata is called transpiration.

<!-- STEP id="column" -->
## A column of water
In the xylem, water forms thin, unbroken columns that run from the roots, up the stem, to the leaves. The water particles in a column hold on to one another.

<!-- STEP id="pull" -->
## The transpiration pull
As water leaves the leaf, the water just behind it is pulled up to take its place, and the whole column moves up a little. This pull is called the transpiration pull, and it helps move water up through the xylem.

**Transpiration is not only a loss of water: it also helps pull water up the plant.**
